prize_parts.citation: for determining the atomic structure of the nitrogenase iron-molybdenum cofactor, including its central carbide, and thereby the structural basis of biological dinitrogen activation
for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand breaks

statement.case_for: I keep nitrogenase (B064) and base editing (B011) as a two-part prize with Rees, Einsle and Liu. After round 1 I have narrowed the nitrogenase citation to what is settled, the atomic structure of the MoFe protein and the FeMo cofactor, including the interstitial carbide that Einsle's atomic-resolution data established. These structures were determined rather than inferred, have been refined and independently confirmed for three decades, and they define the cluster that synthetic and computational chemists now target in ammonia chemistry. Base editing is a different kind of achievement, an enabling method used by a whole community: a deaminase brought to a defined nucleotide, followed by directed evolution of the editors, gives programmed chemical conversion of one base in living cells. In answer to the chair, the chemistry I would honour is the site-specific deamination of a nucleobase and the protein evolution that made it efficient and clean, and not the CRISPR cleavage platform itself. Both parts have a clear technical core, the union is three people, and each part is defensible on its own scientific merits rather than as a compromise.
statement.case_against: Nitrogenase: no other member ranks it first, and the catalytic mechanism and substrate binding are still debated, so the citation must stay on the cofactor structure. That choice leaves out Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe, whose kinetic, spectroscopic and cluster-chemistry work is real, and the three-person cap makes that cost unavoidable. Base editing: the 2020 CRISPR prize is the main framing risk, Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo are not named in a Liu-only part, and off-target and bystander deamination are not fully characterised. A two-part prize that has no second proposer for this exact pairing may also be seen as a compromise, and I have to accept that no configuration, mine included, is near five votes.

responses.point: Brzezinski moved to nitrogenase, wants the citation to rest on the secure cofactor structure and composition rather than the full mechanism, and would add Seefeldt for the biochemical and spectroscopic framework, with Dean and Ribbe weighed explicitly in the expert report.
responses.response: We now agree that the citation should be limited to the cofactor structure, and I have removed the word mechanism from my wording. Where we still differ is Seefeldt. His kinetic and spectroscopic framework is real, but it speaks to turnover, which is the part we both say is not settled, so a structure-anchored citation does not need him. I would accept your three-name list as a nitrogenase-only prize if the committee prefers a single part, and I agree the expert report should weigh Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe by name instead of letting the cap exclude them silently. I would drop Seefeldt only because of the three-person limit across two parts.

responses.point: Somfai asks what is chemically new in base editing beyond biochemical engineering of CRISPR, notes that the 2010 cross-coupling prize and a Crews-only credit make his B058 plus B038 pairing a compromise, and would support nitrogenase if the mechanism firmed up.
responses.response: I take the first point as the main test of B011. My answer is that Liu's work created a new reaction on DNA in cells, the deamination of a specified base in a specified window, and the directed evolution of cytidine and adenine deaminases, including an adenine deaminase that does not exist in nature for DNA, is molecular design. That answers the CRISPR-extension charge better than adoption counts do. On nitrogenase, the mechanism may not firm up soon, but a citation on the structure does not wait for it, in the same way that structure-based prizes in the past did not wait for full mechanisms. On your pairing, I respect B058 as classical chemistry, but I see little support for it, and a Crews-only degrader credit is thinner than the trio that Aili and Chabes propose.

responses.point: Chabes favours Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli for B038 and would put base editing second with a Liu-only credit, accepting that the cereblon glue strand is a competing attribution problem.
responses.response: We agree on Liu alone for B011. On B038, I think the glue strand is a larger attribution problem than a short citation can hide, because the cereblon mechanism explains an existing drug class and is a different discovery from the PROTAC concept. If the committee wants a single-part prize on degraders, I could support the Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli trio only with explicit wording that limits it to heterobifunctional degraders. I keep B038 as an alternative for that reason and because no PROTAC is approved yet. I would ask you whether you accept base editing as the second part of a two-part prize, since your own ballot ranks it second.

responses.point: Aqvist now proposes Liu alone for B011 as the whole prize, citing the originality of the idea, independent worldwide reproduction and the directed-evolution chemistry, while acknowledging the Nishida and Kondo priority question and early clinical benefit.
responses.response: I agree with the Liu-only attribution and with your chemical argument, and I will use it in the citation. I disagree that B011 should be the whole prize. A single-laureate prize for a field that is only about ten years old, with an open Target-AID priority question and a recent CRISPR prize on the same platform, is the least defensible version of base editing, and a second part from a mature, structurally secure field balances it within the three-person cap. If the committee decides to split between two single-laureate options, I would ask you to say whether Rees and Einsle are acceptable to you for the second part.

uncertainties: Whether a nitrogenase part limited to Rees and Einsle can survive the exclusion of Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe once the expert report weighs them.
Whether a majority will accept a two-part prize pairing a structural achievement with an enabling method, since no other member proposes this pairing and no configuration is near five votes.
Whether base editing is seen as distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize and how the Kondo and Nishida priority question is handled in a Liu-only citation.
I cannot verify exact priority and credit claims from the supplied text alone.
statement.conflict_note: I am a colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski at Stockholm University, and my electron crystallography and 3D electron diffraction work is close to the structural methods behind nitrogenase. I have no personal or institutional tie to any credited candidate, and I see no need for recusal.
